rationale: Treesort is a small, pointer-heavy Stanford benchmark whose hot path is recursive tree insertion/traversal with comparison-dominated branches, so the table favors cheap, correctness-safe passes (SUB, SPLIT, IBR) with low cost penalties so they apply broadly, including on the hot sort loop where instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add resistance at negligible runtime/size price; ICALL is strongly favored because indirecting call targets disrupts static call-graph recovery on this compact binary, with only a moderate runtime penalty so it avoids the tightest recursive kernels; BCF and FLA carry high SecurityGain but equally high RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties so the selector restricts them to cold, security-critical functions rather than the comparison-hot traversal path, keeping overhead acceptable on this already branch-dense workload; IGV is retained with high Security/Diversity gain but the strongest RuntimeCost, SizeCost, and CorrectnessRisk penalties (its interprocedural transformations are the riskiest for recursive pointer-manipulating code), letting it fire only where features justify it, and any pass deemed too costly could simply be omitted; overall the weighting maximizes structural diversity (control flow, call targets, inter-block edges) while cost penalties act as the guardrail that keeps total runtime and size inflation bounded and correctness preserved for a recursion- and pointer-intensive program.
